nodes.title: GMI Ultimate Theory Review & Architecture-Prior-Free Derivation Programme
nodes.claim: All material descendants meet their declared evidence requirements.
nodes.inference: Programme closure is the conjunction of required descendant closures.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: Multiple critical scientific descendants remain unresolved.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Any critical descendant remains OPEN or a closed claim loses its evidence.
evidence_required: independent and real-scale evidence where required

nodes.title: Foundations, behavioral quotient, prior boundary, recursive gap core
nodes.claim: The narrow deterministic/symmetry/governance deliverables of #834 are locally reconstructed.
nodes.inference: Analytic proofs plus executable reconstruction close only the declared local surface.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: Independent replication has not been supplied by this package.
nodes.possible_counterexample: A theorem proof fails, validator accepts a hostile mutation, or CI cannot reconstruct.

nodes.title: Symmetry obstruction
nodes.claim: An equivariant deterministic selector at x must choose a stabilizer-fixed hypothesis.
premises: group actions on evidence and hypotheses
nodes.inference: For g in the evidence stabilizer, f(x)=f(gx)=g f(x).
nodes.unresolved_assumption: None inside the stated group-action theorem.
nodes.possible_counterexample: An equivariant deterministic selector chooses a point outside Fix_H(G_x).

nodes.title: Deterministic behavioral quotient and minimality
nodes.claim: Future-behavior equivalence yields a well-defined minimal exact deterministic quotient.
premises: exact equality over every finite action word
nodes.inference: Right-stability makes quotient operators well-defined; exact abstractions cannot merge inequivalent states.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: None inside the stated deterministic exact scope.
nodes.possible_counterexample: An exact deterministic abstraction merges two behaviorally inequivalent states.
nodes.falsifier: A valid countermodel to B1, B2, or B3.

nodes.title: Nondeterministic trace/bisimulation boundary
nodes.claim: Trace equivalence alone does not imply strong bisimulation under nondeterminism.
premises: finite labeled transition systems in N1
nodes.inference: Equal trace sets coexist with an unmatched b/c branching obligation.
nodes.possible_counterexample: The stated p0 and q0 are strongly bisimilar or have unequal trace sets.
evidence_required: finite exact trace and bisimulation reconstruction

nodes.title: Controlled stochastic behavioral quotient
nodes.claim: Identify conditions for canonical/minimal predictive state under controlled stochastic observations.
nodes.inference: Not yet established; deterministic B1-B3 cannot be silently reused.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: Measurability, support, identifiability, approximation metric, and finite-sample conditions are unspecified.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Two latent models induce the same observed predictive tests yet require different claimed quotient states.
nodes.falsifier: A claimed stochastic quotient changes under observationally indistinguishable realizations.

nodes.title: Corpus-wide behavioral-spec/legacy-obligation mapping
nodes.claim: Map all legacy obligation objects to behavior, evidence governance, or non-behavioral metadata without category error.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: The complete corpus has not been classified under the new distinction.
nodes.possible_counterexample: A legacy object called an obligation embeds architecture or evidence state while being treated as pure behavior.
nodes.falsifier: An unclassified or misclassified legacy obligation is found.

nodes.title: Executable architecture-prior leakage detection
nodes.claim: Detect hidden architecture/grammar/search/evaluation priors across derivation and experiment pipelines.
premises: frozen run manifests and source/grammar/search configs
nodes.inference: Disclosure schema exists; automated leakage detection does not.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: No complete instrumentation currently proves absence of undeclared priors.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Twin encodings or search orders change the selected result while the ledger claims invariance.
nodes.falsifier: An undeclared choice changes admissibility or selection.

nodes.title: Independent reconstruction of foundational tranche
nodes.claim: A separate implementation reconstructs S1/B1-B3/N1 and rejects the same hostile mutations.
nodes.inference: Not supplied by the first-party package.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: Implementation independence has not been demonstrated.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Independent implementation disagrees with local outputs or exposes an omitted premise.
